extracted.intended_audience: poets, readers, critics, and students of poetry interested in poetic composition and craft
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on composing lyrical and narrative poems: selecting an appropriate speaking-character, rendering authentic passion, using metre and repetition effectively, and ensuring coherence and apt versification. Includes critical standards illustrated by commentary on The Ancient Mariner and notes on ode-like composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character choice consistent with subject
rubrics_metrics.description: Select a speaker-character whose background and temperament naturally produce the poem's manner of speaking and superstition (e.g., 'a Captain of a small trading vessel ... who being past the middle age of life ... become credulous and talkative ... prone to superstition').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chosen character should be plausible for the ideas and tone expressed; Wordsworth gives the example of an aging small-ship captain retired to a village. Such persons 'have little to do become credulous and talkative'—their predispositions justify the poem's voice and content. Aim for congruence between life-experience and the qualities the poem requires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurately represent traits of superstitious minds
rubrics_metrics.description: Superstitious men are 'almost always men of slow faculties and deep feelings; their minds are not loose but adhesive; they have a reasonable share of imagination ... but they are utterly destitute of fancy.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When portraying superstition, emphasize deep feeling, adhesiveness of thought, and an imagination that composes impressive effects from simple elements rather than relying on fanciful variety. Distinguish imagination (producing impressive effects from simple elements) from fancy (producing surprise by sudden varieties and accumulated imagery).

rubrics_metrics.name: Represent a picture impressive yet consistent with the speaker
rubrics_metrics.description: First object: 'to represent a picture which should not be unimpressive yet consistent with the character that should describe it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance vividness with the narrator's capacities and voice—ensure descriptive richness does not violate the plausible limits of the speaking-character. The picture must move readers yet remain credible as described by that person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convey the speaker's passion to readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Second object: ensure 'words, which in their minds are impregnated with passion, should likewise convey passion to Readers who are not accustomed to sympathize with' such speakers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft diction, rhythm, and imagery so that the narrator's felt intensity transfers to the audience, even when readers do not naturally sympathize with the speaker's temperament. Use techniques that bridge private feeling and public expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use metre to shape perceived motion and passion
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'Lyrical and rapid Metre' to help convey passion and to make a poem that 'in reality move[s] slowly' appear to move quickly by metrical effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploit the musical properties of metre to modulate pacing and emotional intensity: a poem's narrative tempo can be at odds with its metrical energy. Metrical choices can animate slow-moving content and make it feel immediate and impassioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide an introductory piece to set mood when needed
rubrics_metrics.description: An introductory poem may be necessary to give a poem its full effect: 'This Poem ought to have been preceded by an introductory Poem ... an introductory Poem is necessary to give this Poem its full effect.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a work relies on a particular frame of mind or context, include prefatory material or an introductory piece to prepare the reader for tone, voice, or narrative conventions. Omitting such an introduction can reduce the intended impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repetition and apparent tautology can be poetic virtues
rubrics_metrics.description: Repetition is often valuable: 'virtual tautology is much oftener produced by using different words when the meaning is exactly the same' and 'Poetry is passion ... the Speaker will cling to the same words ... repetition and apparent tautology are frequently beauties of the highest kind.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reflexively avoid repeating words or phrases. When repetition arises from genuine feeling, it can reinforce emotional intensity and become an aesthetic asset. Consider the emotional economy of words rather than forcing varied synonyms that mask sameness of meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weigh words by feeling, not by surface variety
rubrics_metrics.description: Words 'ought to be weighed in the balance of feeling and not measured by the space which they occupy upon paper.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize the emotional resonance and efficacy of specific words over inventing different words solely for the sake of variety. The reader's felt response matters more than lexical diversity per se.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid forced synonym substitution (virtual tautology anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using different words when the meaning is exactly the same often creates 'virtual tautology.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize when changing wording for variety dilutes clarity or intensity; prefer repetition or the original phrasing when it best conveys passion. Forced synonym swaps can feel hollow and reduce impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinct characterization for principal person
rubrics_metrics.description: A defect: 'the principal person has no distinct character, either in his profession of Mariner, or as a human being who ... might be supposed himself to partake of something supernatural.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your protagonist has a clear and specific character—occupational, psychological, and moral traits should be delineated so actions and perceptions are believable. Vagueness in the central figure undermines engagement and plausibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure protagonist agency (acts, not only acted upon)
rubrics_metrics.description: A defect: 'he does not act, but is continually acted upon.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the protagonist moments of decisive will or responsibility; even in supernatural narratives, the hero should have agency. Characters who only undergo events without initiative can feel passive and reduce narrative tension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain causal coherence between events
rubrics_metrics.description: A defect: 'the events having no necessary connection do not produce each other.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plot elements should follow logically or psychologically from one another; sequences that feel arbitrary weaken narrative structure. Aim for causes and consequences that make the progression credible or compelling within the poem's world.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-accumulation of imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: A defect: 'the imagery is somewhat too laboriously accumulated.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restrain excessive piling-up of images that may overwhelm clarity or dilute emotional focus. Select and hone images so each contributes meaningfully to tone or theme rather than merely increasing ornament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity of passion (highest merit)
rubrics_metrics.description: A merit: 'the passion is every where true to nature'—authentic passion is a paramount quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The truthful expression of feeling is central to poetic value; genuine emotional truth can redeem other defects. Strive for sincerity and natural feeling in tone, image, and diction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Felicity of language and striking images
rubrics_metrics.description: A merit: 'a great number of the stanzas present beautiful images, and are expressed with unusual felicity of language.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate felicitous phrasing and striking but apt imagery. Elegant expression and well-chosen figures of speech enhance the reader's experience and can elevate passages to memorable effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versification: harmony and artful variety
rubrics_metrics.description: Versification should be 'harmonious and artfully varied, exhibiting the utmost powers of that metre, and every variety of which it is capable.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work the chosen metre thoroughly: vary rhythm, lineation, and sound patterns to keep the verse engaging. Even if a metre seems unsuitable for long forms, artful handling can display its strengths. Pay attention to musical effects, cadence, and formal variety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metre suitability vs. skillful handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Observation: 'the versification, though the metre is itself unfit for long poems, is harmonious and artfully varied.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of the inherent capacities and limits of a metre for a given length or form; when using a metre that might be awkward for long poems, compensate through technical skill—variation, modulation, and musical craft—to maintain interest and appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ode requisites: transitions and impassioned music
rubrics_metrics.description: For ode-like composition: 'the transitions, and the impassioned music of the versification would be found the principal requisites of that species of composition.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In odes and similarly elevated lyric forms, prioritize fluid, meaningful transitions and the musical intensity of versification. The shift between sections and the poem's sustained musicality are key to fulfilling the form's expectations.
